If a continuation line is encountered before any `-1` line (malformed/truncated FRD file), the variable is read uninitialized, which is undefined behavior. Since this declaration is being touched anyway, initialize it to 0 to make the change safe.

Consider collapsing the whole `#if/#elif/#else` chain into a single `printf("number of vertices = %zu\n", nvertices);` and applying the same fix to `PythonStuff.cpp` (note the 32-bit branch currently passes a `std::size_t` to `%d`, which is a signed/unsigned mismatch).

comments.content: The cast only converts `M_PI`; the `2.0` literal is still `double`, so the product is evaluated in `double` and the result is narrowed back to `float` on `+=`. This means the conversion the patch is meant to remove (narrowing double→float, as checked by `cppcoreguidelines-narrowing-conversions` in `.clang-tidy`) still occurs. Use a `float` literal so the whole expression stays in `float`. The same applies to the two `endangle += 2. * static_cast<float>(M_PI);` occurrences in this file.

comments.content: All the new `%ld` specifiers are paired with `DWORD` arguments (`size`, `result` here, and later `entry.lineNumber`, `gle`, `symOptions`, `ver.dwMajorVersion/dwMinorVersion/dwBuildNumber`, `v1..v4`). `DWORD` is `unsigned long`, so `%ld` is still a signedness mismatch: it is technically UB and, unlike MSVC, clang/GCC `-Wformat` will still complain about it. Since these values are unsigned, `%lu` is the exact match and silences the diagnostics on all toolchains.

Use `%lu` — same applies to the other new `%ld` specifiers in this file (`entry.lineNumber`, `gle`, `symOptions`, `ver.dw*`)."
